title: Famous ancient sites and monuments by country

source.name: Wikidata (CC0)
source.method: sparql:SELECT ?item ?itemLabel ?article ?sitelinks ?countryLabel WHERE { { SELECT ?item (SAMPLE(?c) AS ?country) (COUNT(DISTINCT ?c) AS ?nC) WHERE { ?item wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q839954 ; wdt:P17 ?c ; wikibase:sitelinks ?sl . FILTER(?sl >= 25) } GROUP BY ?item } hint:Prior hint:runFirst true . FILTER(?nC = 1) OPTIONAL { ?article schema:about ?item ; schema:isPartOf <https://en.wikipedia.org/> . } ?item wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks . SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en,mul". } } ORDER BY DESC(?sitelinks) LIMIT 160

country.match: Match each ancient site to its country.
country.odd: Three of these ancient sites are in {value}. Which one isn't?

rows.label: Troy
rows.description: ancient Homeric-era city in northwest Asia Minor; it is known as the setting for the Greek myth of the Trojan war
rows.hook: was besieged for a full decade in a war fought over a stolen queen, according to legend

rows.label: Colosseum
rows.description: ancient Roman amphitheatre, a landmark of Rome, Italy
rows.hook: hosted gladiator battles and mock hunts for cheering crowds of ancient Romans

rows.label: Machu Picchu
rows.description: 15th-century Inca citadel in the Peruvian Andes and UNESCO World Heritage Site
rows.hook: sat hidden in the mountains for centuries before explorers stumbled upon it

rows.label: Constantinople
rows.description: capital of the Eastern Roman, Latin and Ottoman Empires, currently Istanbul, Turkey
rows.hook: straddled two continents as an empire's capital, guarded by legendary walls

rows.label: Stonehenge
rows.description: Neolithic henge monument in Amesbury, Wiltshire, England, UK
rows.hook: aligns perfectly with the sunrise on the summer solstice for reasons still debated

rows.label: Göbekli Tepe
rows.description: neolithic archaeological site in Turkey
rows.hook: is considered one of the oldest known temple complexes built by human hands

rows.label: Pompeii
rows.description: ancient Roman city near modern Naples, Italy
rows.hook: was buried by a catastrophic volcanic eruption that preserved it in ash

rows.label: Pantheon
rows.description: ancient Roman temple in Rome, Italy
rows.hook: features a massive dome with an open hole at its very center

rows.label: Sparta
rows.description: city and city-state in ancient Greece
rows.hook: trained its citizens from childhood to become the ancient world's fiercest warriors

rows.label: Great Pyramid of Giza
rows.description: oldest and largest of the three pyramids in the Giza Necropolis; one of the seven ancient wonders of the world
rows.hook: served as a pharaoh's tomb and was the tallest man-made structure on Earth for millennia

rows.label: Athens
rows.description: capital and largest city of Greece
rows.hook: is often called the birthplace of democracy and Western philosophy

rows.label: Angkor Wat
rows.description: Hindu-Buddhist temple complex in Cambodia
rows.hook: began as a Hindu temple before becoming a Buddhist site of pilgrimage

rows.label: Damascus
rows.description: capital and largest city of Syria
rows.hook: is often called one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world

rows.label: Petra
rows.description: ancient rock-cut historical city in Jordan
rows.hook: was carved directly into rose-colored cliff faces by ancient traders

rows.label: Carthage
rows.description: historical city in Tunisia
rows.hook: was home to the general who marched war elephants across the Alps to invade Rome

rows.label: Terracotta Army
rows.description: collection of ancient Chinese military statues
rows.hook: was buried alongside an emperor to protect him in the afterlife

rows.label: Parthenon
rows.description: former temple of Athena on the Athenian Acropolis, Greece
rows.hook: was built as a temple honoring a goddess of wisdom and war

rows.label: Cairo
rows.description: capital city of Egypt
rows.hook: sits near some of the world's most famous ancient pyramids

rows.label: Acropolis of Athens
rows.description: ancient citadel above the city of Athens
rows.hook: rises above its city as the hilltop fortress where its most sacred temples were built

rows.label: Cologne
rows.description: most populous city in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
rows.hook: gave its name to a perfume made from citrus and herbs

rows.label: Alexandria
rows.description: port city on the Mediterranean coast of Egypt
rows.hook: was home to an ancient library said to hold the world's collected knowledge

rows.label: Hadrian's Wall
rows.description: defensive fortification in Roman Britain
rows.hook: marked the northern edge of an empire's territory across the island of Britain

rows.label: Chichen Itza
rows.description: pre-Columbian Maya city in Mexico
rows.hook: was built so a shadow shaped like a serpent creeps down its steps each equinox

rows.label: Jericho
rows.description: city in West Bank, Palestine
rows.hook: appears in an ancient story where its walls collapsed after trumpets were sounded

rows.label: Teotihuacan
rows.description: ancient Mesoamerican city
rows.hook: was built by a civilization whose very name and identity remain unknown

rows.label: Xi'an
rows.description: capital of Shaanxi Province, China
rows.hook: was the starting point of the ancient trade route linking east and west

rows.label: Ithaca
rows.description: Greek island in the Ionian Sea
rows.hook: was the homeland a legendary wanderer spent a full decade trying to return to

rows.label: moai
rows.description: monolithic humanoid figures
rows.hook: are massive stone figures carved with oversized heads on a remote Pacific island

rows.label: Rhodes
rows.description: island in Aegean sea, Greece
rows.hook: stood beside a giant bronze statue considered one of the ancient world's wonders

rows.label: Mycenae
rows.description: ancient city, now an archaeological site in Argolis, Greece
rows.hook: was ruled by the legendary king who led the Greeks against Troy

rows.label: Temple of Ephesian Artemis
rows.description: temple in Ephesus, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World
rows.hook: was burned down by a man seeking fame for the act of destroying it

rows.label: Egyptian pyramids
rows.description: ancient masonry structures constructed by ancient Egyptians
rows.hook: come in over a hundred different sizes scattered up and down the Nile valley

rows.label: Nineveh
rows.description: ancient Assyrian city, capital of the Neo-Assyrian Empire
rows.hook: was the Assyrian capital where a king assembled the first known royal library

rows.label: Antioch
rows.description: ancient Greek city in southern Turkey
rows.hook: was the city where followers of a new faith were first called by a name still used today

rows.label: The Great Sphinx
rows.description: ancient Egyptian monumental sculpture
rows.hook: is a giant statue with the body of a lion and a human face, missing its nose

rows.label: Uruk
rows.description: ancient city of Sumer and Babylonia
rows.hook: is home to the legendary king whose adventures were recorded in the world's oldest surviving epic

rows.label: Persepolis
rows.description: ancient city in Marvdasht County, Iranian national heritage site and World heritage site
rows.hook: was burned to the ground by a conquering Macedonian king's army

rows.label: Mohenjo-daro
rows.description: archaeological site in the province of Sindh, Pakistan
rows.hook: had advanced drainage and plumbing systems long before most other ancient cities

rows.label: Buddhas of Bamiyan
rows.description: sculptures in Afghanistan before 2001
rows.hook: were carved into a cliffside as some of the tallest standing statues of their kind

rows.label: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
rows.description: one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World
rows.hook: was such a grand tomb that its builder's name became a word for grand tombs everywhere

rows.label: Delphi
rows.description: ancient town in Fokida, Greece
rows.hook: was home to a priestess believed to deliver prophecies from a god

rows.label: Tyre
rows.description: city in the South Governorate of Lebanon, also an ancient Phoenician city and the legendary birthplace of Europa and Elissa (Dido)
rows.hook: gave its name to a rare purple dye once worth more than gold

rows.label: Knossos
rows.description: ancient Minoan through Roman administrative center and city
rows.hook: is linked to a legendary maze built to contain a half-bull, half-man beast

rows.label: Nazca Lines
rows.description: large geoglyphs made in the soil of the Nazca Desert in Peru
rows.hook: are giant desert drawings of animals only fully visible from high in the air

rows.label: Syracuse
rows.description: Italian municipality
rows.hook: was the home of a mathematician who famously ran through the streets shouting "eureka"

rows.label: Lascaux
rows.description: cave in southwestern France famous for its Paleolithic cave paintings
rows.hook: contains prehistoric paintings of animals that have survived for many millennia

rows.label: Giza pyramid complex
rows.description: archaeological site on the Giza Plateau, Egypt
rows.hook: brings together several ancient tombs and a giant statue on one desert plateau

rows.label: Trier
rows.description: city in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany
rows.hook: stands behind a massive black stone gate raised by ancient conquerors

rows.label: Memphis
rows.description: ancient capital of Egypt
rows.hook: was the political capital of an ancient kingdom near its famous pyramids

rows.label: Herculaneum
rows.description: Roman town destroyed by eruption of Mount Vesuvius
rows.hook: was destroyed by the same volcanic eruption that buried a more famous neighboring town

rows.label: Valley of the Kings
rows.description: necropolis in ancient Egypt
rows.hook: holds the tombs of pharaohs, including one found nearly untouched by looters

rows.label: Pergamon
rows.description: ancient city of Ionia in modern-day Turkey and UNESCO World Heritage Site
rows.hook: is credited with inventing a writing material as a substitute for scarce papyrus

rows.label: Çatalhöyük
rows.description: archaeological site in Konya Province, Turkey
rows.hook: is considered one of the very first large settlements where humans lived closely together

rows.label: Castel Sant'Angelo
rows.description: castle and museum in Rome, formerly the imperial mausoleum of the emperor Hadrian and subsequent Roman emperors
rows.hook: began as an emperor's tomb before becoming a fortress connected to a secret escape passage

rows.label: Great Zimbabwe
rows.description: ruined city in the south-eastern hills of Zimbabwe near Lake Mutirikwe and the town of Masvingo, was once the capital of the Kingdom of Zimbabwe during the country's Late Iron Age
rows.hook: was built entirely from stacked stone without any mortar holding it together

rows.label: Borobudur Temple
rows.description: Buddhist temple in Java, Indonesia
rows.hook: is arranged as a giant mandala meant to be walked as a spiritual journey

rows.label: Roman Forum
rows.description: Ancient Roman center of the city, a landmark of Rome, Italy
rows.hook: was the marketplace and government center at the heart of an ancient empire's capital

rows.label: Thebes
rows.description: ancient Egyptian city
rows.hook: was a religious capital dedicated to a powerful sun god

rows.label: Palatine Hill
rows.description: centremost of the seven hills of Rome, Italy
rows.hook: is the legendary birthplace of a city, according to a myth about two brothers raised by a wolf

rows.label: Ctesiphon
rows.description: capital of the Iranian empire in the Parthian and Sasanian eras in present Iraq
rows.hook: was home to the largest brick archway built without any reinforcing supports

rows.label: Ellora Caves
rows.description: ancient cave temples of Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism in Maharashtra, India
rows.hook: was carved out of solid rock into a hillside complex of Hindu, Buddhist and Jain shrines

rows.label: Abu Simbel
rows.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site in southern Egypt
rows.hook: has two rock-cut temples guarded by colossal statues of a pharaoh, moved to save them from a rising dam lake

rows.label: Palmyra
rows.description: ancient city in Homs Governorate, Syria
rows.hook: was a caravan oasis ruled by a warrior queen who challenged Rome, famed for its colonnaded street

rows.label: Tikal
rows.description: ruins of major ancient Maya city
rows.hook: is a rainforest city of towering stepped pyramids rising above the jungle canopy, once a major Maya power

rows.label: Karnak Temple Complex
rows.description: ancient Egyptian temple complex
rows.hook: is a vast sacred site near Luxor with a forest of giant columns in its Hypostyle Hall

rows.label: Merv
rows.description: archaeological site in Turkmenistan
rows.hook: was a great Silk Road oasis city and one of the largest in the medieval world

rows.label: Chauvet Cave
rows.description: cave in France
rows.hook: is famous for some of the oldest and most stunning prehistoric paintings of lions, horses and bison

rows.label: Olympia
rows.description: town on the Peloponnese peninsula in Greece, site of the ancient Olympic Games
rows.hook: was the sanctuary where the original Games in honor of Zeus were held and the Olympic flame is lit today

rows.label: Susa
rows.description: ancient city in Iran, World Heritage site in Iran
rows.hook: was an ancient capital of the Persian Empire where a famous law code stele was found

rows.label: Leshan Giant Buddha
rows.description: monumental sculpture
rows.hook: is a towering stone carving of a seated holy figure beside a river, the tallest of its kind in the world

rows.label: Harappa
rows.description: archaeological site in Punjab, Pakistan
rows.hook: was a major city of the Bronze Age Indus Valley civilization, with planned streets and drainage

rows.label: Nalanda Mahavihara
rows.description: ancient Hindu-Buddhist monastery in present-day Bihar, India
rows.hook: was a famed ancient Buddhist center of learning that drew scholars from across Asia

rows.label: Pont du Gard
rows.description: ancient Roman aqueduct bridge that crosses the Gardon River in Vers-Pont-du-Gard, France
rows.hook: is a tall three-tiered Roman aqueduct bridge that carried water across a river valley

rows.label: Caesarea Maritima
rows.description: ancient Levantine city
rows.hook: was a port city built by King Herod, later the Roman capital of the province of Judea

rows.label: Baalbek
rows.description: city in Baalbek-Hermel, Lebanon
rows.hook: is home to some of the largest Roman temple columns ever built, including a temple to Jupiter

rows.label: Hattusa
rows.description: capital of Hittite empire
rows.hook: was the mighty fortified capital of the Hittite empire, with a famed Lion Gate

rows.label: Mesa Verde National Park
rows.description: U.S. national park in Colorado
rows.hook: preserves spectacular cliff dwellings built into canyon walls by the ancestral Pueblo people

rows.label: Byblos
rows.description: Mediterranean city in the Mount Lebanon Governorate, Lebanon, a main Canaanite-Phoenician city
rows.hook: claims to be one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities and gave its name to the word for Bible

rows.label: Miletus
rows.description: ancient city of Ionia, in modern-day Turkey
rows.hook: was the birthplace of Greek philosophy and home to Thales, with a large surviving Roman theater

rows.label: Taxila
rows.description: archaeological site of the ancient Indian subcontinent, at Taxila, Punjab, Pakistan
rows.hook: was a renowned ancient center of learning, visited by Alexander the Great on his march east

rows.label: Thermopylae
rows.description: ancient fortified passage in central Greece
rows.hook: is the narrow coastal pass where 300 Spartans made their famous last stand against a Persian army
